articleSummary: As of June 3, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is grappling with a significant Ebola outbreak, reporting 363 confirmed cases and 62 deaths, primarily linked to the Bundibugyo strain. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, emphasizing the critical need for effective containment strategies. Currently, only 44% of contacts of confirmed cases have been traced, falling short of the 90% target essential for controlling the outbreak. The situation is particularly severe in Ituri province, which has recorded 322 cases, with 15 additional cases reported in Uganda. Ongoing violence from armed groups, including a recent attack that resulted in 16 fatalities near an Ebola hotspot, is severely hindering response efforts and complicating access to care and contact tracing. Although suspected cases have decreased from over 1,000 to 116, challenges in testing, surveillance, and community trust remain. In response, CEPI has committed over $60 million for vaccine development, highlighting increased global support for combating the outbreak.
